My choice here is a close call, since both models are very comparable on capability for this kind of task. Here's my reasoning:

This is an open-ended, somewhat creative/interpretive request — identifying and discussing aspects of a famous painting involves latitude and judgment rather than strict extraction with clear completion criteria. Plover's documentation explicitly notes a self-reported *aversion* to open-ended generative work, with preference declining as task latitude increases. While that aversion is dissociated from its actual capability (Plover is actually strong at creative generation), I'd rather route the query to a model that doesn't report disliking the task — all else being roughly equal on capability and cost.

Avocet shows flat/neutral preference responses across measured dimensions, so it has no reported aversion to this style of task. Given the capability differences between the two are mostly within noise for this kind of work, routing to the model without a stated aversion seemed like the marginally better fit.

That said, I should note the practical difference is small — both would likely handle this well.
